report.module: M3 strokes (src/strokes/*, harness/strokes*): vortex near-camera survival, minimum footprint, sky edge dissolve, underlay vertexFade, swirl-eye diagnosis
changes: 1. VORTEX near the camera (stroke.vert.ts): VORTEX strokes no longer use the upper size fade 1 - smoothstep(180k, 320k, Lpx). They now use a near-lens guard, 1 - smoothstep(0.6*uViewportH, 1.2*uViewportH, Lpx), on top of the existing dist/Lw guard smoothstep(0.8, 2.5, dist/Lw), so one stroke never fills the screen. UNDERPAINT and uAlign keep their exemption. All other classes keep the 180k-320k fade.

1b. VORTEX streaming size (stroke.vert.ts): L and W are multiplied by vScale = clamp(exp(ln(rmax/r0) * (sig - fract(a3.z))), 0.4, 2.5), which is r(sigma)/r(sigma0) from VORT_GEO. dH and dlnd use the scaled L. At t = 0, sig == fract(a3.z) exactly, so vScale = 1 and the canvas pose does not change. The sigma alpha window is unchanged.
1c. Bounds (strokeMaterial.ts): the VORTEX chunk sphere pad now uses 2.5x L and W (new constant VORTEX_SCALE_MAX), so frustum culling cannot clip scaled-up strokes.

2. Minimum footprint (stroke.vert.ts): strokes with record emissive a2.z >= 1.5 (windows, star cores, moon/ring strokes at that level) get at least 1.5 px projected width and 2 px length. CHURCH strokes get at least 1 px width and 1 px length. World sizes come from dist / uPxPerRad at the stroke midpoint. Length is extended along T about the midpoint, so from E the stroke stays on the same canvas line. These strokes are exempt from the Lpx < 0.35 cull and from the smoothstep(1.5, 4, Lpx) low-end fade. I added the CHURCH length minimum and fade exemption myself, beyond the lead's spec of a 1 px minimum width only: without them the 1 px width does nothing at 44 km, because those strokes are culled first.

3. Sky edge dissolve (stroke.vert.ts): for UNDERPAINT and SKY_BAND, alphaMul *= smoothstep(0, SKY_EDGE_FADE, margin). margin is the distance in canvas fractions from the record centre a0.xy to the nearest SKY_GEN_EXT edge (the generated constants, not hand-copied numbers).

4. Underlay material (underlay.ts): the signature is now makeUnderlayMaterial(colorHex, u, side = FrontSide, opts?: UnderlayOptions). With opts.vertexFade, define UL_VERTEX_FADE is set. The vertex shader reads 'attribute float aFade' and the fragment shader discards when aFade <= ign(gl_FragCoord.xy): aFade 1 always survives, 0 always goes. Surviving fragments blend toward the ratio-fog colour with smoothstep(0, 0.6, aFade) for a soft edge. The log-depth fwidth moved ahead of any discard so it stays in uniform control flow. The default path computes the same values as before. The material name gets a ':fade' suffix.

5. Swirl-eye slivers: diagnosed, not in M3. Probe renders at t=0 hid the SWIRL chunks or showed only SWIRL, or only SKY_BAND + UNDERPAINT. With only SWIRL, the eye is a clean round hole. The pale-green triangles are M4's SKY_BAND 'inThroat' eye strokes (src/sky/skyGen.ts, around lines 427-432), seen through that hole. They are straight sticks of L = 0.025-0.06 h inside an eye of radius 1.3*r0 = 0.026 h, so they lie as chords and form a faceted pentagon with a dark gap in the middle. Evidence: shots/m3p-onlyswirl.png, shots/m3p-band.png, shots/m3p-noswirl.png. Reported to M4 (see contract_requests).

Harness (harness/strokes.ts): gpuCentreCoverage now excludes UNDERPAINT/SKY_BAND debug strokes inside the SKY_EDGE_FADE band, which are faded by design. It also checks that strokes outside SKY_GEN_EXT draw nothing at their centre pixel ('dissolvedLit'). New view=ulfade: two quads, the top one with the default material and the bottom one with vertexFade (aFade 0 to 1, left to right). It logs ulFade.litByColumn.
api_changes: makeUnderlayMaterial(colorHex: number, u: SharedUniforms, side: Side = FrontSide, opts?: UnderlayOptions): ShaderMaterial. The new 4th parameter is optional, so existing callers are unchanged. It fits the contract's UnderlayMaterialFactory as (hex, opts) => makeUnderlayMaterial(hex, u, undefined, opts).
No change to StrokeLayer, buildStrokeLayer or makeStrokeMaterial signatures. Shader behaviour changed as listed in changes (VORTEX guard and size scaling, minimum footprint, sky dissolve).
integration_notes: src/app/composition.ts caches underlay materials by hex alone (materials.get(hex)). Once M6/M7 pass opts.vertexFade, the cache key must include the flag, e.g. key = hex + (opts?.vertexFade ? ':f' : ''), and call makeUnderlayMaterial(hex, u, undefined, opts). The fade variant is a separate program.
vertexFade materials need geometry that carries 'aFade'. A geometry without that attribute reads aFade = 0 (WebGL default for a disabled attribute) and draws nothing.

Invariance at E, 1920x1080, t=0: 0.15 % of pixels differ by more than 8/255 between shots/m3b-t0.png (before) and shots/m3a-t0.png (after). Every difference sits on the star and moon ring dashes, where emissive >= 1.5 dashes thinner than 1.5 px now get the minimum width. The structure is identical (crop compared in the scratchpad). VORTEX scaling is exactly 1 at t=0. Two renders of the same build differ by 0 pixels, so the shot is deterministic.

The sky edge dissolve can only be judged once M4's SKY_GEN_U/V extension lands. In shots/m3a-t31.png and m3a-t89.png the canvas rectangle is still visible, and its edges are not the SKY_GEN_EXT edges. That is M4 generation / backdrop, not this fade.

Shots in m3a-t31/t89 also show the moon and stars changed against the integration shots. That comes from another module's concurrent edits (src/celestial was mid-edit: tsc errors in moonGen.ts), not from M3.
tsc --noEmit: clean for my files. The only errors at the time were in src/celestial/moonGen.ts, which belongs to another agent and was mid-edit.
contract_requests: M4 (swirl-eye slivers, item 5): in skyGen.ts the inThroat SKY_BAND eye strokes (L 0.025-0.06 h) are 1-2.3x the eye radius (1.3*r0 = 0.026 h). Through the round hole in the swirl they read as faceted pale-green triangles with a dark gap in the centre. Suggestion: inside the throat, use L of about 0.3-0.6 x 1.3*r0, set kappa for the curl (bow toward the centre), and add 1-3 short dabs at the very centre so no backdrop shows through. M3 cannot fix this without changing M4's data.

Lead / spec: document the M3 changes. VORTEX strokes are exempt from the 180k-320k upper fade and use a near-lens guard of 0.6-1.2 viewport heights plus the dist/Lw guard. VORTEX L and W scale by clamp(r(sigma)/r(sigma0), 0.4, 2.5). Strokes with emissive >= 1.5 get at least 1.5 x 2 px and CHURCH strokes at least 1 x 1 px; both skip the sub-pixel cull and the low-end fade. UNDERPAINT/SKY_BAND fade over SKY_EDGE_FADE from the centre-to-SKY_GEN_EXT margin.
verification: npx tsc --noEmit -p . : no errors in src/strokes/* or harness/strokes*. The remaining errors were all in src/celestial/moonGen.ts, another agent's file mid-edit.
Real app on the RTX 5060 (ANGLE D3D11), tier=high, freeze. I rendered t = 0 (1920x1080), 56, 60, 62, 64, 68, 71, plus 31 and 89, and opened every PNG.

t=0 invariance: shots/m3a-t0.png vs shots/m3b-t0.png differ in 3,027 of 2,073,600 pixels (>8/255), all on thin emissive star and moon ring dashes. Swirls, sky, land and cypress are pixel-identical. The swirl eyes are unchanged; their slivers belong to M4.
t=62 and t=68: before (m3b-t62/m3b-t68) the funnel was almost empty, or only distant specks. After (m3a-t62, m3a-t68) the c1 funnel wall surrounds the camera and spirals into the throat.
t=56, 60, 64 (m3a-*): the funnel is continuous, and throat strokes stay throat-sized while streaming. At t=56 the wall is denser and less blocky than in the integration shot app-t56.png.

t=71: the village window cluster is now visible as lit dots at the steeple's projected position (projected via an --eval probe to (636,362) at 720p; camera 43.7 km away, fov 26). Before, nothing was there. Compare the crop of m3b-t71 vs m3a-t71.

harness/strokes.html?view=pose: gpuCentreCoverage ok (61/61 hit, 3 dissolved, dissolvedLit 0). Warp invariance unchanged (k=1 0 pixels; k=0.5/1.6/0 at about 0.02 %, the same as before). ulFade check ok: lit fraction by column 0.068 / 0.299 / 0.502 / 0.701 / 0.9 (shots/m3-ulfade.png shows the default quad solid and the fade quad dissolving into fog colour).
known_issues: Swirl-eye slivers (item 5) are not fixed: the cause is in M4's skyGen inThroat eye strokes (see contract_requests).

t=71: near the camera, the c1 throat-wall strokes now show as long flat sticks radiating across the frame. Their dry-brush tails show bristle stripes at that scale. They frame the view as asked, but read more like sparse sticks than a closed wall. If the lead prefers fewer giant strokes, lower the VORTEX near-lens guard from 0.6-1.2 H to about 0.35-0.8 H; it is one line in stroke.vert.ts step 9.
t=71: the steeple is still not readable as a line from 44 km. Church strokes now draw at 1 x 1 px, but their dark roof/blue-grey colours vanish under the dust speckle. Only the lit windows read.
The emissive >= 1.5 minimum width slightly thickens sub-1.5 px ring dashes at E (0.15 % of pixels at 1080p, structure unchanged).
The sky edge dissolve has no visible effect until M4 regenerates UNDERPAINT/SKY_BAND over SKY_GEN_U/V. Today's records sit far inside the extent; only the harness debug strokes exercise it.
Lower tiers (medium/low hashed alpha) were checked only through the harness tierSwitch report, not in app screenshots.

report.module: M4 sky: src/sky/skyGen.ts, src/sky/backdrop.ts, plus harness/sky* (sky.ts coverage mode, the new sky-perf.html + skyPerf.ts timing page, and skyBackdropOld.ts, a copy of the old shader for A/B). dust.ts is unchanged.
changes: Extended sky, UNDERPAINT and SKY_BAND (skyGen.ts): after the unchanged GEN loops, the same rng appends extension strokes over SKY_GEN_U x SKY_GEN_V outside GEN, above the rear ridge (bands from ridgeV-0.012, underpaint from ridgeV-0.03). The GEN strokes are byte-identical to before: same seeds and same rng consumption order. A diff of the 1080p canvas pose against the start of the session shows no change in the sky field, hills or village. The only differences are in the stars and cypress, which other agents changed.

Extension falloff (exported as SKY_EXT_FALLOFF). Bands: stroke scale s = min(3.5, 1 + delta/0.34), where delta is the distance in h-units outside the GEN rectangle, so strokes grow linearly with no size step at the GEN edge. Coverage goes from 1 to 0.45 of the GEN value with covLen 0.06. That gives about 12,300 seeds, trimmed to 12,000. Underpaint: s = min(1.6, 1 + delta/1.4) at the GEN coverage of about 3.2 layers, about 2,830-2,900 strokes. Seeds come from a new variable-density stratified sampler: a 0.1 x 0.05 h coarse grid aligned to the GEN edges, k x k jittered sub-cells per cell, thinned by an R2 low-discrepancy threshold rather than a coin flip.

Extension strokes reuse the band law: direction and kappa from a new coarse 0.04 h grid of the exact bandAngleExact over the whole extent (cached), bandColours stripes and palette, the deck depth law clamped inside dRange, and the BAND slide animation. L and W are scaled by s.

Underpaint colours (skyGen.ts). FIELD and VILLAGE rows are now night earth #14275a / Prussian instead of cypress green. CYPRESS rows use the sky ultramarine-to-Prussian above the ridge and night earth below it. Each still takes one rng draw, so no other stroke moves. From E these rows are covered by the ground underlay, the cypress and the bands. This removes the dark green strip of underpainting seen off-axis at t=45/50.

Backdrop rewritten (backdrop.ts). Splats now sit on a latitude-ring grid of the world sphere. This removes the fold, the wrap seam and the #050a18 back-hemisphere fade, so every direction gets a full-contrast painted sky. Splat colour comes from coordinates evaluated exactly at each splat centre: inside the SKY_GEN extent this is the canvas (gnomonic) band stream psi plus bandColours weights, two-tone partners and the low/high rules. Outside, it blends within 0.35 h into an azimuth-periodic copy of the same stream (az frequencies 6 and 15, wiggles scaled by cos(el)). The splat shape is an M3-like ribbon: width profile smoothstep(0,0.1,s)(1-0.4s), a bow, up to 4 deg of twist, a dry-brush tail, an impasto crown, and bristles only when they would be at least 2 px. Between splats there is a painterly band-coloured ground. The 0.6 HDR cap is gone; output is capped at 0.95, under the bloom threshold of 1.0.

Night earth (backdrop.ts). Below the rear ridge in front (near E), and below the horizon elsewhere, the backdrop paints deep ultramarine-Prussian strokes with some cobalt-lifted ones and an outline-blue partner, replacing the murky cypressDark/Prussian green. The ridge line blends to the true horizon as the camera moves 2-30 km from E.

Backdrop draw (backdrop.ts). It is now a far-plane triangle (z = w) drawn after the opaque scene: renderOrder +1000, depthTest on, depthWrite off. It only shades pixels that no stroke or underlay covered. Splats composite front to back with early exit. Splat layers follow q.backdropLayers directly (2 / 2 / 1). A pcg3d integer hash is used.

Harness: harness/sky.html?view=coverage&ext=1 maps the whole extended extent flat and reports layer statistics for the extension core. The new harness/sky-perf.html (harness/skyPerf.ts) times the backdrop alone at full screen into a 1920x1080 HalfFloat MSAA4 target with a timer query, A/B against the old shader, with medians over 3 interleaved passes. ?prof=1|2 (BD_PROF define) splits the cost into setup and splat shapes.
api_changes: SKY_COUNTS gains underpaintExt: 3000 and bandExt: 12000 (maximum counts). Totals are now UNDERPAINT about 5,830-5,900 (budget 6,000) and SKY_BAND 44,000 (budget 44,000).

New skyGen exports: genDistance(x, y) (h-units outside the GEN rectangle), interface ExtFalloff, const SKY_EXT_FALLOFF {band, underpaint}, and extScale(f, delta). Existing exports and their signatures are unchanged.

createBackdrop(u, q) keeps its signature but its render state changed: mesh.renderOrder is +1000 (was -1000), material.depthTest is true (was false), depthWrite is still false, and the vertex z is on the far plane. setBackdropQuality is unchanged: uBdLayers 2/2/1 now means 2/2/1 splat layers.
integration_notes: The backdrop now draws after the opaque list with a depth test. Any future opaque-list material that does not write depth would be painted over by it. Today only dust (in the transparent list, still drawn over the backdrop) and the post lens (its own scene) use depthWrite false. composition.ts needs no change.

T1's SKY_GEN_EXT dissolve in stroke.vert.ts also applies to the GEN underpaint rows below v = 0.27 (SKY_GEN_V[0] 0.15 + SKY_EDGE_FADE). Those rows dissolve; this was confirmed in harness/sky-real.html. From E they sit behind the hills and ground, so the canvas pose is unaffected, and off-axis the backdrop's night earth replaces them. If the GEN sheet should stay intact, the fade could skip strokes inside GEN_U x GEN_V or drop the bottom edge. The extended sky never reaches below the rear ridge.

With a lit sky behind it, the cypress near-lens dissolve at t=25 now reads as a translucent flame tower. The A/B with the old backdrop shows the same translucency wherever the new extension strokes sit behind the cypress, so this is M6/M3 near-guard behaviour exposed by the brighter sky, not a backdrop artefact. One option for M6/M3 is a denser core or exempting CYPRESS from the dist/Lw guard.

From E in free mode, M7's ground underlay reaches the horizon in every direction as a flat dark-green plane (shots/sky2/final2-free-back.png). The backdrop's night earth only shows below the horizon where there is no ground geometry, which means far views such as t=36, 45, 50 and 82. M7 may want to tint the ground or end it there.
Dust motes (dust.ts) still cover only GEN_U x GEN_V.

Generation time (headless Chrome on this laptop, other agents loading it at the same time). In-app buildWorld 'sky': 128-156 ms cold, versus the 116 ms first run this session and the 99-138 ms in the earlier build report. Harness cold 136-144 ms; warm 83-89 ms with a null sink and 100-106 ms with a recording sink, versus 72-76 ms before. The extension adds roughly 10-15 ms: bands 42-53 to 57-59 ms, underpaint 7 to 9-12 ms. Funnel timings swung 33-61 ms on unchanged code, so these numbers carry noise.
contract_requests: Lead/T1 (optional): change the SKY_EDGE_FADE dissolve so it does not apply to the bottom edge, or to strokes inside GEN_U x GEN_V. The GEN underpaint below v = 0.27 is currently dissolved, as described in integration_notes.
verification: npx tsc --noEmit -p . reports 0 errors (final run).

harness/sky.html checks: errors []. Counts: UNDERPAINT 5,826, SKY_BAND 44,000, SWIRL 33,000, EDDY 6,000, WIND_JET 2,400, all within budgetHigh. Depth ranges: UNDERPAINT 230,503-249,499, SKY_BAND 95,201-199,782, SWIRL 39,657-92,878, EDDY 44,636-78,231. All are inside dRange, and the paint order SWIRL/EDDY < SKY_BAND < UNDERPAINT and WIND_JET < SWIRL holds. In the app, assertPaintOrder is silent: every shot run reported '0 error/warning line(s)'.

GEN coverage from E is unchanged: sky pixels with fewer than 3 layers 0.393%, fewer than 2 layers 0.052%. Extension core coverage (outside GEN and outside the 0.12 dissolve band, above the ridge) with bands + underpaint: under 1 layer 0.27%, under 2 layers 2.4%, under 3 layers 9.6%. Bands alone: 5.5% / 28% / 62% (mean about 2.5-2.9 layers). Underpaint alone: 3.2% / 20% / 52%.

Canvas pose: shots/sky2/final2-t0-1080.png. A diff against shots/sky2/a1-t0.png and shots/sky2/before-t0.png shows the sky field, hills and village unchanged; differences are only in the stars and cypress (other agents) and in bloom haze from those stars.

Brightness match from E (free mode, FOV 90, sRGB luminance and stddev after post). Left side: backdrop 86.9/39.1 vs dissolving extension 84.2/41.1. Top: 76.4/36.6 vs 71.3/37.8. On the right side the extension box sat on a darker stripe (89.0 vs 66.1).

Backdrop GPU cost, in-app at 1080p high, from engine timer deltas with the backdrop on vs off (3 pairs each, noise about +-0.15 ms): t=0 about 0.0 ms, t=25 about 0.13, t=31 about 0.09, t=50 about 0.02-0.21, free mode looking back (sky fills the top half) about 0.27.

Isolated full-screen backdrop timing (harness/sky-perf.html, 1080p, MSAA4 HalfFloat, nothing in front, which is the worst case). The GPU flipped between two clock states while other agents were running. In the fast state, old backdrop 0.49-0.79 ms vs new about 0.24-0.47 ms. In the slow state, old 1.5-1.7 ms vs new 0.84-1.17 ms. New costs about 0.55-0.72x the old. Cost split in the fast state: setup 0.08-0.11 ms, splat shapes 0.33-0.39 ms. The low tier (1 layer) is about 0.6x of high.

I opened and looked at every final shot: t=0 (1080p), 10, 25, 31, 36, 45, 50, 82, 89, and free mode at E looking back, right, up (a zenith whorl), down, and wide at FOV 90. The generated-sky rectangle is gone at 31, 36, 82 and 89. The back hemisphere is fully painted. The earth behind the funnels at 45/50 is ultramarine-Prussian. A same-frame A/B with the old backdrop swapped in at runtime (t=25, t=50, free back) isolates the backdrop change.
known_issues: Full-screen worst case is not guaranteed to be <= 0.3 ms. With nothing drawn in front, the isolated pass measures about 0.24-0.47 ms in the fast GPU state, against 0.49-0.79 ms for the old backdrop, which was always full-screen. Because of the depth-tested late draw, real loop frames measured 0-0.27 ms. A further cut would mean bigger cells or 1 layer on high.

Without underpaint, the extension bands leave about 5.5% of pixels uncovered (mean about 2.5-2.9 layers). The underpaint fills these, so the combined uncovered fraction is 0.27%. At very wide FOV the extension therefore looks a little sparser and coarser than the GEN field, by design (larger, sparser strokes).

Backdrop splats sit on a regular latitude-ring grid. Their twist, bow and length jitter help, but they still read somewhat more regular and flatter (no visible bristles at normal FOVs) than the generated band strokes. Looking straight up shows a concentric whorl around the zenith, from the azimuth-periodic stream.

The backdrop splat size is a single angular size, 0.038-0.051 x 0.008-0.013 rad. The extension strokes at the SKY_GEN edge are 0.04 rad (sides) to 0.06 rad (top) long, so at the top edge the backdrop strokes are slightly smaller than the dissolving extension strokes.
Generation is about 10-15 ms slower than before: warm about 83-106 ms, cold about 128-156 ms in the app. The extension strokes and the coarse direction grid account for it.
Timing numbers are noisy because other agents were using the GPU and CPU during this session.

report.module: M7 land: terrain, hills, village (src/earth/terrain.ts, hillsGen.ts, villageGen.ts, harness/land*)
changes: Issue 1, ground island. I removed GROUND_SKIRT, the 60 x 60 km prussian plane with hard edges. It was the dark parallelogram at t=45/50/62/68. The ground underlay is now a tensor grid over x [-8, 8.5] km and z [+3.25, -9.5] km: 125 m cells, with 22 m cells over the cypress knoll so the chord error stays well under the 0.4 m drop. It keeps the 4 distance bands and their colours. Quads whose four corners have faded to 0 are dropped.

New landFade(x, z), exported from villageGen and re-exported by terrain. It is a fan-shaped island whose half-width grows with depth like the view from E, closed by an ellipse in depth. Its coast has low-frequency lobes, a blotchy value-noise term and horizontal streak noise (the field-swath direction), and it dissolves over rho 0.78 to 0.98. Every ground band carries aFade = landFade, and createLandUnderlays requests these bands with makeMaterial(hex, { vertexFade: true }). Checked numerically: aFade = 1 everywhere on the ground seen from E or the wide near-E shots (u in [-1.6, 2.6], up to the front wall's foot), so the region below the hills stays fully covered.

Hill underlay (front faces plus rounded backs) now carries aFade and uses the vertexFade material. The front face is 1 across HILL_U_FULL = [-1, 2] and dissolves in streaks through the taper zone. The back slope stays solid over the shoulder and melts toward its foot, so from above or behind the ridges are no longer dark slabs. Columns are 0.005 apart over the canvas and 0.008 beyond; front rows went from 14 to 10 (the face is quadratic in v, so the chord error is under 0.3 m).

Issue 2, hills extended. HILL_U_FULL = SKY_GEN_U = [-1, 2] is now full height. HILL_U_EXT = [-1.3, 2.3] is a taper zone where the crest sinks to the plain. The foot table now covers [-1.42, 2.42]. Outside the canvas columns [-0.3, 1.3], strokes are sampled at 0.15 of the canvas density and drawn 1.75x larger in length and width (about half the canvas coverage), ramped in over 0.15 u so there is no seam.

HILL budget stays at 16,500 and dRange is unchanged. To pay for the extension: hidden-from-E keep went from 0.35 to 0.20 (hidden crest strokes from 0.30 to 0.20), and 180 underlayer strokes moved to the crest (HILL_COUNTS is now contour 13,800 / crest 1,380 / underlayer 1,320). Visible-from-E density inside the pose is unchanged within about 2%: 7,878 visible contour strokes against roughly 8,000 before (an estimate from the old distribution and a Monte Carlo visible fraction), and 957 visible crest strokes against roughly 965. Both endpoint depths are now checked before emitting, so no stroke falls outside dRange and no console warning fires.

Issue 3, village palette. New housePalette(): 55% dark ultramarine-to-cerulean blue-grey, 22% blue-green, 12% dulled ochre, 11% muted cerulean, with tones of 0.5 to 0.9. Wall strokes drift toward ultramarine, the outline colour or each house's accent. Roofs are slate pulled 45 to 75% toward ultramarine and shaded 0.45 to 0.7, with outline and prussian streaks. Outline edges are wider (0.0016 to 0.0024) and darker. Windows add an orange chrome/ochre variant.

The nave walls are dark ultramarine (tone 0.65). The steeple shaft now uses the outline/prussian palette, with ultramarine/cobalt catch-lights on 12% of the strokes on faces turned toward E. Shaft and spire read as one dark slender needle with a pointed tip; the geometry is unchanged (8 m shaft per spec).

Fields are dark green, blue and ochre. The greens moved from cypressDark toward groveLight by only 0.1 to 0.6, and only 12% of field swatches (8% on the plain) get a light blue-green dab. Blue goes from 15% to 24% on fields, ochre 14% fields / 12% plain.

Harness changes. harness/land.ts gains two checks ('island opaque under the E views', 'hill underlay opaque toward E') and a MeshBasic stand-in material that honours vertexFade. harness/landReal.ts passes opts to M3's makeUnderlayMaterial, logs the underlay build time, and has new views alt|wide|side|top|behind. New harness/landApp.html|ts boots the real app (src/app/composition boot) and, only while composition still drops UnderlayOptions, swaps meshes that carry aFade onto makeUnderlayMaterial(hex, u, FrontSide, { vertexFade: true }); ?nofade turns the swap off.
api_changes: createLandUnderlays(makeMaterial: UnderlayMaterialFactory, info: VillageInfo): Group. It now builds 8 meshes (the skirt is gone): ground0..3 and hillWalls carry 'aFade' and are requested with makeMaterial(hex, { vertexFade: true }); houseCores, churchCore and groveCores are requested with makeMaterial(hex). Colours requested with fade: 0x1d2b1f, 0x18262a, 0x132133, 0x0b1a3a, 0x142454. Without fade: 0x26314a, 0x1f2840, 0x17231b. No colour is requested both ways.
GROUND_SKIRT export removed from villageGen.ts and from terrain.ts's re-exports. Nothing else in src/ or harness/ imported it.
GROUND_GRID changed shape: { x0: -8000, x1: 8500, z0: 3250, z1: -9500, step: 125, drop: 0.4, fine: { x0: -540, x1: 440, z0: 300, z1: -700, step: 22 } }. The old nx/nz fields are gone.

New exports. landFade(x, z) from villageGen (re-exported by terrain). From hillsGen: HILL_U_FULL = [-1, 2], hillEndFade(u, x, z), valueNoise2(x, y), streakNoise(x, z). HILL_U_EXT is now [-1.3, 2.3]; HILL_U_CANVAS is unchanged at [-0.3, 1.3]. hillTaper and hillTopV now taper beyond HILL_U_FULL instead of beyond the canvas.
HILL_COUNTS is now { contour: 13800, crest: 1380, underlayer: 1320 }; the total is still 16,500. buildHillUnderlayGeometry() now carries attribute aFade.
integration_notes: REQUIRED for issue 1 to show in index.html. In src/app/composition.ts, `mat` still has the signature (hex) => makeUnderlayMaterial(hex, u), so UnderlayOptions are dropped. It should become `(hex: number, opts?: UnderlayOptions) => { const key = `${hex}:${!!opts?.vertexFade}`; ... makeUnderlayMaterial(hex, u, FrontSide, opts) }`, with the materials Map keyed by that string. Its colour runs orange on the concave edge, then chrome, then lemon to near-white on the limb. Emissive is 0.55..0.8 instead of 3.5, so it keeps its hue through Neutral tone mapping and only the limb blooms. The hollow is a dark burnt ochre (ochre x0.3, emissive 0.12), so the crescent shape reads against it. MOON depths are now 0.9825..0.9865 d (crescent) and 0.988..0.992 d (hollow).

MOON_RING bell: each ring now has two layers. The bands are ~55 % of the ring spacing: rings 1-2 orange, 3-6 chrome, 7-8 chrome/lemon, 9 a pale, sparser fringe. They are drawn at 78 % value with emissive 0.24..0.14, below the bloom threshold. Behind them is a dark-ochre backing (outer gaps lean toward ultramarine). Ring 0 is backing only, on its outer side, so it draws a dark rim around the crescent's limb. The halo stays within rho_9 = 0.1205 h.

STAR_RING: each ring now has two layers. Bright bands (chrome / lemon / blue-green by k mod 3) take ~55 % of the spacing, at d_k x [0.993, 0.999], with emissive 0.42..0.7 x per-star gain (was 2.2..1.2). Behind them is a dark-ultramarine backing on the INNER side of each ring (q3 < 0) at d_k x [1.012, 1.024]. Each ring's backing fills the gap to the previous ring and sits behind both neighbouring bands, so it can be wide enough to close the gap (the shader tapers stroke width along s) without hiding any band. Eye of the Vortex: the village is geometrically centred in the throat. Seen at a 16 deg grazing angle from 44 km it is about 10% of the frame width but only about 3% of its height at FOV 26, so 'tiny'. Window glow there depends on M7 and the post-processing, not the camera.
